Yep, I tested this on the RBMC prototype with ~3000 PEL files, including both full-sync and background-sync scenarios, and it worked fine in my testing. I did not observe any inconsistencies.
This should probably all be hidden behind a meson option so other users don't incur any costs.
Do you mean to put this all logic behind a meson option so it’s only enabled for RBMC use cases? I can update it accordingly.
yea.
Acknowledged
Will failure to create watcher descriptor for an error file result in termination of application due to abort() ?
Yes I also agree, we could handle gracefully throwing a runtime exception instead, Impact is restoration of Synced PELs wont work automatically until restart the application

My initial thought was to treat this as fatal because even though the synced files will still be present on disk, without the watcher they won’t get restored into D-Bus until some later restart. My concern was the live D-Bus state, because any client watching the interface or property changes could miss those entries completely, and we do not really control for the phosphor-logging when that next successful restart will be. So I was leaning more toward fail-fast here instead of silently running. what do you think about that tradeoff?

>what do you think about that tradeoff?


The biggest concern here is ,systemd will attempt to restart the application, and if all retries fail, the BMC could transition to a quiesced state. That might be a relatively heavy in this scenario i feel.

Do we really want to mark the BMC as quiesced due to a failure in creating the watcher? 

@rameshi1@in.ibm.com Could you please share your view?

The likelihood of inotify_init1 failing is low. In such a case, we can throw an exception that propagates to the main function, causing the application to crash and trigger a restart. If it fails again, the system can retry once more, after which the BMC would transition into a quiesced state.

Ideally, we should not ignore this failure silently, as certain functionalities (such as sync refresh) would not occur. Since this is part of the event log setup, it is important to explicitly flag the failure.

Also, this inotify initialization should be performed only when the redundant BMC feature is enabled.

Yes, I would treat it as a fatal failure.

It is expected to be a very rare case, and in that worst-case scenario it should also generate a dump to help with debugging.
Same doubt as above.

For safer, size of buffer can keep as per inotify manpage, it says:

Specifying a buffer of size `sizeof(struct inotify_event) + NAME_MAX + 1` will be sufficient to read at least one event.

Reference : https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html

My thinking here was to use a larger buffer so one callback can drain multiple queued inotify events, instead of processing only one event per iteration. Since this runs under sdeventplus, a smaller buffer would still be functionally correct because the callback will continue firing while the fd remains readable, but it may require more iterations during bursts of synced files (for example, during full sync) i was mainly thinking about the performance side here.

Haa got it, that's good..

I hope bigger buffer wont cause partial read of events.
Yes it should be always buffer_size / event_size.

Sure. Based on the man page, `sizeof(struct inotify_event) + NAME_MAX + 1` is about 272 bytes, which is enough for one worst-case event.

So I can keep the buffer at `65280` bytes. In the worst case, that gives room for about 240 events in a single read.

I like this check, but what happens if:
1. BMC A creates event.
2. event is synced to BMC B
3. someone updates Resolved property on BMC A.

Actually this case is handled by the refresh flow introduced in another commit.

When a property like Resolved is updated on BMC A and synced to BMC B, the corresponding file change triggers the refresh path (refreshFromDisk), which updates the in-memory entry on the peer.

inotifyFD --> It's an inotify instance (actually a FD), but can setup multiple path watches, so generic could be better.

errDirWatcherWD --> we are watching the error directory, rather than individual files inside.

That makes sense. since this inotify FD is specifically used for the error directory watcher, plain inotifyFD feels a bit too generic here. How about `errDirInotifyFD`? I also have another inotify FD in the PEL path, so this would help keep the two uses distinct.
